# Check commit metadata

A composite action every repository of mine runs as one step of the CI job it
already has. It fails when a commit of the pull request:

- is not authored by me (the `name` and one of the `emails` inputs);
- is committed by anyone but me or GitHub. GitHub is the committer of the
  "Update branch" button and of edits made in the web editor, so both work;
- has a `Co-Authored-By` trailer, a line starting with "Generated with" or
  "Generated by", or a line starting with "Requested by ... thread". Lines
  are matched at their start, after any markup, so prose that mentions
  "generated by" mid-sentence passes;
- links to one of the `blocked-domains`, or to a subdomain of one.

Pull requests that Dependabot opened may also carry Dependabot's commits
(`allow-dependabot`). Who opened the pull request comes from GitHub, not from
the commits, so a commit that only claims to be Dependabot's fails anywhere
else. Their messages are still checked.

## What it does not cover

It checks commits only; the PR description is not checked. CI does not run
again when the description is edited, so a result about it would go stale.
The description is reviewed by hand before merging.

## Use

In the job that already runs on `pull_request`, after or before any step:

```yaml
      - name: Check commit metadata
        uses: Abrunacci/infra/.github/actions/check-commit-metadata@<full commit SHA> # main
```

Pin it to a full commit SHA of this repository, like any other action. The
step needs nothing else:

- **No checkout.** It fetches the pull request's commits (commits only, no
  files) into a throwaway repository with the job's own token, so the job's
  checkout can be shallow, sparse, or missing, and the workspace is left
  untouched.
- **No extra permission.** `contents: read` is enough, for public and private
  repositories.
- **On a push to main** it prints that there is nothing to check and passes:
  what lands on main was checked as a pull request.

The defaults of the inputs in `action.yml` are the policy for every
repository, so changing it is a pull request here; each repository picks the
change up when its pinned SHA is updated.

## Run it by hand

`check_authorship.py` uses only the standard library. From a clone that holds
both commits:

```sh
python3 .github/actions/check-commit-metadata/check_authorship.py \
    --base origin/main --head HEAD \
    --name "Alejandro Brunacci" --email abrunacci87@gmail.com \
    --blocked-domain claude.ai
```

It exits 0 when every commit passes, 1 with every problem and how to fix it,
and 2 when git cannot read the commits.

## Tests

The tests build real git repositories, including one that serves the pull
request's head only under `refs/pull/1/head`, as GitHub does, and run the
action's own shell step with its default inputs.

```sh
python3 -m venv .venv && . .venv/bin/activate
pip install -r tests/check-commit-metadata/requirements.txt
pytest tests/check-commit-metadata
mypy --strict .github/actions/check-commit-metadata/check_authorship.py tests/check-commit-metadata
```
